Frequently Asked Questions: Dry Sift Hash
What is dry sift hash?
Dry sift is a solventless cannabis concentrate made by mechanically separating trichomes (resin glands) from cannabis flower using screens, without using ice water, heat, or solvents. The collected trichomes are often pressed into flat plates or slabs.
What does “Cali plate” style mean?
“Cali plate” refers to a presentation style and quality tier that became popular in the concentrate market — hash pressed into flat, thin plates. It’s more of a branding/style term than an official product standard, so quality varies significantly between producers regardless of the name.
Is dry sift hash the same as bubble hash or rosin?
No. Bubble hash uses ice water and agitation to separate trichomes; rosin uses heat and pressure on flower or hash to extract oil. Dry sift uses only dry mechanical sifting through screens, which typically retains a bit more plant material than bubble hash but no solvents at any stage.
How is quality typically judged?
By trichome purity (how little plant debris is present), texture (malleable, not crumbly or dry), color, aroma intensity, and melt quality when heated. A certificate of analysis (COA) from a third-party lab is the only reliable way to verify potency and check for contaminants like pesticides or mold.
How should it be stored?
Cool, dark, airtight conditions — similar to flower. Heat and light degrade terpenes and potency over time.
Is it legal to buy?
This depends entirely on your local jurisdiction. Cannabis concentrate legality varies by country and, in the US, by state. It’s worth checking local law before purchasing anything, and buying only through licensed retailers where required.
How can I verify a specific product’s claims?
Ask for a current, batch-specific COA from an accredited third-party lab — not just a claim of “lab tested” on a website. Legitimate producers make these easy to find.

Purity is lower, potency varies batch to batch, and there’s rarely any lab testing behind it.

What is dry sift hash?

How does it differ from ice-water hash or frozen sift?
Ice-water hash and frozen sift both use cold and moisture, and typically finish as soft, pliable, crumbly resins that need moderate humidity in storage. Dry sift starts from cured material, stays completely dry throughout, and is pressed firm. It carries a more classic, earthy, traditional hash character, whereas water-based resins tend to be brighter and fresher on the nose.

Around 190–210°C. Dry sift benefits from marginally more heat than fresh-frozen resins, which are best kept below 200°C. Begin at the lower end with a cold start and adjust upward until you find the balance of flavour and vapour you prefer.

Warm a blade under hot water or briefly over a flame, dry it, then slice. The heated edge cuts through cleanly. Attempting to break a cold slab by hand tends to send fragments across the table.
How should I store it?
Cool, dark, airtight, and dry. Glass is ideal. Keep it away from radiators, sunlight, and damp environments. Pressed dry sift stored properly will hold up for a very long time.
Do I need a humidity pack?
No, and please don’t use one. Unlike ice-water hash or frozen sift, pressed dry sift wants genuinely dry conditions. Added moisture softens the slab, harms melt quality, and creates a risk of mould over time.
Can I press it further or make it into a temple ball?
Yes. Dry sift responds well to gentle warmth and hand pressure, and many people enjoy working it further to change the texture and deepen the aroma. Work slowly with low heat; overheating drives off the terpenes you’re trying to concentrate.

Frequently Asked Questions: La Mousse Jealousy Hash
What is Jealousy hash?
It’s a dry sift hash made from the Jealousy strain, a hybrid whose genetics trace to Sherb Bx1 and Gelato 41. It refers to the strain used to produce the hash, not a hash-making method itself.
What does “La Mousse” mean?
La Mousse isn’t a single strain — it’s a hash style. The name (French for “foam/mousse”) describes a soft, light, airy texture, distinct from denser, firmer pressed hash. Many different strains, including Jealousy, get made into this style.
How is it made?
Through dry sifting — a solventless, mechanical process that separates trichomes (resin glands) from cannabis flower using screens, without ice water, heat, or chemical solvents.
What does it taste and smell like?
Commonly described as earthy with pine and herbal notes, balanced by sweetness, fruit, and citrus, with a slightly gassy edge — reflecting the underlying Jealousy strain’s terpene profile.

How potent is it compared to flower?
Hash concentrates trichomes, so it’s generally more potent by volume than raw flower. Reports describe this style as fairly strong, meaning a small amount tends to be noticeable.
How should it be stored?
Cool, dark, and airtight. The mousse-style texture is more delicate than firmer pressed hash — heat, light, air exposure, and over-drying can degrade its texture and aroma faster.
Is “La Mousse” an official grade or certification?
No — it’s a style/branding term, not a regulated standard. Quality and authenticity vary a lot between producers and sellers, regardless of how a product is labeled.
How can I verify potency or purity claims?
Ask for a current, batch-matched Certificate of Analysis (COA) from an accredited third-party lab — covering potency and contaminant screening (pesticides, solvents, heavy metals, microbials) — rather than relying on a seller’s description.
